topic: Why the foot‑in‑the‑door technique can backfire in friendships

script.title: Foot-in-the-door technique backfires in friendships – why?
script.hook: Why does a tiny favor ruin friendships?

scenes.text: Why does a tiny favor ruin friendships?

motion_action.headline: Why does a tiny favor ruin friendships?

scenes.text: The foot-in-the-door trick nudges you to say yes.
Studies show compliance rises about thirty percent after a small request.

motion_action.label: increase in compliance after small request

scenes.text: But friends value autonomy; forced agreement triggers reactance.

motion_action.statement: Friends value autonomy; pressure sparks reactance

scenes.text: Reactance makes them reject future asks, even harmless ones.
A 2020 meta-analysis found the effect doubles when the favor feels obligatory.
So a simple 'yes' can become a silent resentment seed.

motion_action.headline: A simple yes can breed silent resentment

scenes.text: Notice when a friend says yes too quickly.
Pull back, give space, and let the balance restore.
Now you know why a small ask can backfire:

script.description:
Why does a tiny favor ruin friendships? Discover the hidden downside of the foot-in-the-door technique.
Learn how compliance can trigger reactance.
Spot the signs before it harms your bonds.
